title: Pinegrove Health — privacy & VPC integration probe (scratchpad)
content:
Meeting 2025-02-14 (intro call)
Attendees: Dr. Nisha Rao (Pinegrove CTO), Samir Desai (SRE), Leanne Ortiz (PM), Ava Chen (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood Solutions)

High-level ask
- Pinegrove Health wants an LLM-backed clinician assistant for triage notes and care-plan suggestions. Must not send raw PHI to multi-tenant hosted endpoints.
- Prefer a Private deployment (VPC + customer-managed control plane) but open to a staged PoC on Hosted API if data is pseudonymized.

Primary constraints (non-negotiable)
- No plaintext patient identifiers leave their VPC (names, MRNs, SSNs).
- Data residency: initial rollout in eu-west-1 only.
- Auditability: every inference request must be logged (request id + model version + token counts) to a customer-accessible audit stream for 180 days.
- KMS integration required for model keys and any cached KV store. HSM optional but requested for final contract.

Performance targets
- 99th percentile latency for single-turn triage (250 token prompt, 200 token response) < 500ms for interactive UI. This is optimistic but their UI team wants snappy feedback.
- Sustained throughput target for pilot: 40 qps during clinic hours, with bursts to 120 qps for batch triage windows.
- Cost target: pilot budget ~ $6k / month for inference (they will tolerate overspend within reason during PoC).

Integration notes / architecture options discussed
1) Private deployment (preferred):
   - Redwood Private with customer VPC peering, control plane in their account.
   - Model execution in a dedicated subnet with egress locked down.
   - KMS integration: bring-your-own-key (BYOK) for model cache encryption.
   - Audit logs -> S3 (encrypted) + CloudWatch/EventBridge forwarding.

2) Hosted API (PoC path):
   - Pseudonymize identifiers at client side (hash MRN + salt) and only send PSIs.
   - Use short TTL for prefix cache and ensure cached tokens are not PHI-bearing.
   - Explicit opt-in for streaming to avoid sending whole contexts.

Gotchas & fragility points raised in call
- Tokenization drift: their existing prompt templates are EMR-extracted and contain non-UTF punctuation; we need to run a tokenization audit for the chosen model family to avoid token-count surprises.
- KV cache leakage risk: if we cache user-specific prefixes, must guarantee encryption + access controls. For hosted PoC, avoid caching patient-specific prefixes altogether.
- Fallback behavior: they want deterministic fallback to a smaller quantized model when capacity constrained, but also need to guarantee not to downgrade to a model that increases hallucination risk on clinical text. Need eval set.
- Streaming timeouts: their frontend closes WebSocket after 8s; we need to tune chunk size or force early partials.
- PII scrubbing false-negatives: will need conservative post-processing and a manual review queue.

Sample prompt pattern (for prototyping)
- system: "You are a clinical assistant. Extract problem list, suggested care-plan bullet points with evidence links to the chart. Do not include patient identifiers. If you are not sure, say 'insufficient data'."
- user: "ED note: [redacted note text]"
- assistant: (structured JSON: problem_list:[], care_plan:[], confidence_score:0-1, evidence_refs:[])

Note: they asked explicitly for structured JSON outputs rather than free text to simplify downstream consumption. Discussed function/tool calling vs schema enforcement — team prefers strict JSON with light schema validation in the runtime.

Observability / eval needs
- Per-route token-cost breakdown + tracer that surfaces which prompt fragment generated most tokens (helpful for prompt optimization).
- Quality monitoring: compare suggested care_plan items against gold triage set (we need 200 labeled examples).
- Regression alerts: if hallucination rate (precision of extracted problems) drops by >5% vs baseline, trigger rollback.

Security checklist items to validate for Private deploy
- VPC peering requirements and IAM roles (Samir to provide network CIDR + existing peering configs)
- KMS key ARN + rotation policy
- S3 endpoints and bucket policy template for audit logs
- Egress rules + NAT gateway avoidance (they want no general internet egress)

Open questions (to resolve before demo)
- Will Pinegrove allow using pseudonymized data for Hosted PoC? If yes, who owns the salt and how is it stored? (action: Leanne to confirm)
- What is the acceptable maximum latency for the UI? 500ms P99 feels aggressive; can we get them to accept 800–1000ms for PoC? (action: Ava to raise with product UX)
- Which model family do they want as baseline? We suggested an Llama-variant (2x8B) quantized + a 13B fallback. Need sample outputs to verify hallucination profile.
- Audit log location and retention: 180 days requested — confirm their legal can accept S3 + Glacier lifecycle.

Action items / next steps
- (Ava) Produce a short runbook for Hosted PoC pseudonymization patterns + sample client-side sanitizer — due 2025-02-18.
- (Marcus) Prepare a Private deployment checklist with required network artifacts and a template IAM policy — due 2025-02-21.
- (Leanne) Confirm data residency + legal sign-off on using pseudonymized test records for PoC — due 2025-02-19.
- (Samir) Share VPC CIDR, permitted egress list, and KMS key ARN (if BYOK) — due 2025-02-17.
- (Pinegrove) Provide 200 labeled triage examples (anonymized) for baseline eval — requested in to Leanne by 2025-02-25.

Quick PoC plan (staged)
- Week 0: alignment + NDA + legal sign-off for PoC data flows.
- Week 1–2: Hosted PoC with pseudonymized data (short sample set), lightweight UI integration, produce initial quality metrics.
- Week 3–4: Private deployment runbook + pilot in customer VPC (limited capacity nodes), run 200-example eval, tune caching & streaming.

Notes to self (SE style)
- Bring up tokenization audit script (tokenizer-checker.py) and run against their exported EMR notes.
- Prepare model-variant regression matrix with hallucination risk notes (will need ML/R&D help).
- Watch out for telemetry gaps: ask infra to expose per-request duration broken down by kernel (attention, matmul, io).

Meeting artifacts to attach later
- Confluence: pinegrove-poc-design (placeholder)
- JIRA: PI-790 (PoC epic)
- Sample policy templates: s3-audit-bucket-policy.md, redwood-kms-byok-template.md

Tone: keep this doc rough — share with Marcus and Jonas before sending the PoC runbook to Pinegrove.

-- Ava
